subject: Business
title: The Ansoff Matrix: Where to Grow
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Ansoff Matrix: Where to Grow.

hook.text: Should you sell more of what you have or launch something new? Igor Ansoff built a matrix to decide.

buildup.text: Four growth paths: market penetration, market development, product development, and diversification.

discovery.text: Market penetration is safest — sell more to existing customers. Diversification is riskiest — new product, new market.

twist.text: Most companies overestimate their ability to diversify. They assume competence in their current market transfers.

climax.text: Amazon diversified from books to AWS — it worked because cloud computing leveraged existing infrastructure.

punchline.text: Grow where your strengths apply. The further you stretch, the more you risk.

quiz.question: What is the riskiest growth strategy in the Ansoff Matrix?
options: Diversification — new products in new markets
Market penetration — more sales in current markets
Product development — new products in current markets

details.summary: The Ansoff Matrix maps four growth strategies by combining existing and new products with existing and new markets: market penetration, product development, market development, and diversification. Each quadrant carries increasing risk, with diversification being the riskiest growth strategy.
details.whyItMatters: Growth is not one strategy but four distinct alternatives with different risk profiles. The Ansoff Matrix helps companies systematically evaluate growth options and allocate resources appropriately based on their risk appetite and capabilities.
takeaways: Market penetration sells existing products to existing markets with lowest risk
Diversification combines new products and new markets with highest risk
Each growth quadrant requires different capabilities and investment levels

faq.question: When should a company pursue diversification despite its risk?
faq.answer: When existing markets are saturated or declining, when the company has excess resources and capabilities transferable to new markets, when synergies exist between current and new businesses, or when risk reduction through portfolio diversification outweighs the execution risk.

faq.question: What is the difference between related and unrelated diversification?
faq.answer: Related diversification enters new markets that share resources or capabilities with existing business, like Disney expanding from films to theme parks. Unrelated diversification enters completely different markets, like a conglomerate adding unrelated businesses.
